messages:
alex.m: ALB target group for edge-gpu-pool in us-west-2 spiked Unhealthy around 02:10 UTC and a ton of pod IPs were deregistered. I'm seeing IPv6 addresses in the target list which seems wrong. Anyone on this?

infra-bot: [alert] target-group arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111222333444:targetgroup/tg-0a1b2c3d marked 28 targets Unhealthy (HealthCheckFailed)

priya.k: Which TG and service? any recent cluster/CCM upgrade? :thinking:

ben.s: TG: tg-0a1b2c3d, service = svc/edge-gpu (kube-system). We upgraded EKS control plane and nodes last night to 1.26 and enabled dual-stack feature gate.

sasha: do `kubectl get endpoints svc/edge-gpu -n kube-system -o wide` — are endpoints dual-stack (v4 + v6)?

ben.s: ran it, output shows pods with both 10.0.45.12 and fd00:10:0:45::12

alex.m: AWS console shows target IPs registered as IPv6 for that TG (odd, TG was created before dualstack). I think CCM started registering pod IPs including v6.

priya.k: ALBs in our private VPC subnets are IPv4-only; they can't reach pod IPv6 unless we have route/translator. Is the TG marked IPv6? run `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn>` to see target addresses.

ben.s: pasted output (short):
```
Targets: { Id: "fd00:10:0:45::12", Port: 8080, Health: Unhealthy }
Targets: { Id: "10.0.45.12", Port: 8080, Health: Healthy }
```

sasha: that explains the failures — ALB probes hitting IPv6 entries from control-plane/CCM but ALB path to IPv6 is broken in our private subnets. CCM must be registering both families and TG prefers v6 addresses.

alex.m: How do we fix quickly? We need targets back to Healthy and stop deregistrations.

priya.k: Temporary fix: force the service annotation to register only ipv4 targets: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-ip-version: "ipv4"` then patch svc. That should re-register TG with IPv4s only.

ben.s: preparing patch now, will `kubectl annotate svc/edge-gpu -n kube-system service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-ip-version=ipv4` then restart CCM reconcile if needed.

alex.m: Also open a support case with AWS about TG behavior on dual-stack clusters. If CCM tries to register v6 by default that's a bug/compat issue.

sasha: long-term: either enable IPv6 routing in VPC (route tables + egress gateways) or set CCM preference to ipv4. We should also add an e2e test for TG registration dual-stack behavior.

ben.s: patch applied at 02:28 UTC, TG shows only IPv4 targets now. Healthchecks turning green. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: [incident] #INC-2026-124 created: dualstack-alb-healthchecks — assigned to eng-infra

priya.k: filing postmortem and we should document to avoid accidental dual-stack ON for edge clusters until infra is ready. I'll own the postmortem.

alex.m: thanks team. followups: (1) AWS case, (2) add a cluster upgrade checklist step for dual-stack, (3) e2e test + CCM config change. I'll create tickets.

aws-ccm-bot: CC: cloud-controller-manager logs show `RegisterTargets: registered ip family: ipv6` after node update (log snippet saved to /var/log/ccm/ccm-2026-03-18.log)

ben.s: adding note: we did not see conntrack or SNAT port exhaustion this time — root cause is target IP family mismatch. Closing thread once postmortem done.

priya.k: PTAL at the postmortem draft in #incidents. :eyes:

alex.m: closing for now, reopen if any regression.
